{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZlj-UQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhDMGQw", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 101, "title": "Delay preconfigured NTSC combined H/V IRQs with HTIME=0 to master clock 10", "body": "## Problem

Combined H/V timer mode (`NMITIMEN & $30 == $30`) with HTIME=0 currently asserts IRQ immediately when entering the matching scanline. The repository’s specification reconciliation identifies assertion ten master clocks later. This can wake WAI and expose TIMEUP too early.

At baseline `c6d12caa8a0e5d4eb66c1ca88e94d55ee6de68d2`, [SystemBus::tick](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/c6d12caa8a0e5d4eb66c1ca88e94d55ee6de68d2/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L195) excludes HTIME=0 from delayed horizontal assertions, then explicitly asserts it at rollover. Existing tests preserve this approximation:

- `machine.rs::combined_zero_timers_retain_approximate_rollover` expects offset zero.
- `horizontal_irq_tests.rs::horizontal_irq_zero_and_late_controls_retain_only_approximate_scheduling` expects combined zero to assert at H=0.

These expectations must be corrected rather than treated as hardware requirements. This implements the incomplete behavior prioritized by the supplied latest assessment; the supplied open-Issue list contains no duplicate.

## Expected outcome

For NTSC non-interlaced operation, with combined mode and HTIME=0 established before entering the selected scanline:

- VTIME selects the matching scanline.
- With no earlier IRQ pending, TIMEUP bit 7 remains clear at elapsed master H=0 through H=9 and asserts at H=10.
- Natural V=0 rollover, ordinary lines, the alternating short V=240 line, and its following line use the same ten-clock offset.
- Nonmatching lines and unreachable VTIME values do not generate this event.
- Existing pending-flag retention, read acknowledgement, access-end sampling, and CPU service after DMA remain the emulator’s current conventions.

The numerical basis is the **SNES Timing H/V Events** detailed list in [Fullsnes](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm): combined HTIME=0 uses H=2.5 timer units, hence `2.5 × 4 = 10` master clocks. It is a special case; applying the nonzero horizontal rule would incorrectly produce 14 clocks. [Anomie’s Register Doc, revision 1157](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gilligan/snesdev/master/docs/snes_registers.txt), NMITIMEN/HTIME/VTIME/TIMEUP, supplies complementary register and comparison descriptions.

These source distinctions are recorded in [Issue #99’s reconciliation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/c6d12caa8a0e5d4eb66c1ca88e94d55ee6de68d2/docs/issue-99-validation.md#source-reconciliation-recorded-before-implementation) and [Issue #97’s contract](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/c6d12caa8a0e5d4eb66c1ca88e94d55ee6de68d2/docs/issue-97-validation.md#specification-and-bounded-contract). Their terse equality descriptions do not establish immediate assertion. Fullsnes’s acknowledgement-window qualification and Anomie’s older TIMEUP write-clear wording remain unresolved; this Issue does not claim to settle them.

## Context and reproduction

Only repository files and supplied context were inspected for this plan. External specifications were not independently retrieved, tests were not rerun, and no files were changed. The hardware contract above rests on the repository’s recorded source reconciliation.

A focused counterexample using the existing private bus-test helpers is:

1. Create `timer_bus(0x30, 0, 1)` before entering V=1.
2. Advance 1363 master clocks: TIMEUP should be clear.
3. Advance one clock to V=1/H=0. Current behavior sets TIMEUP; expected behavior leaves it clear.
4. Using independent fresh observations, check H=9 clear and H=10/H=11 pending.

Correct only preconfigured combined HTIME=0 delivery and its supporting tests/documentation. Reuse the existing scheduler structure and original guest-building patterns where appropriate.

H-only HTIME=0, late line-spanning horizontal delivery and VTIME ownership, live timer configuration, physical reset/startup alignment, TIMEUP write/coincident-read behavior, instruction-level interrupt recognition, NMI delay, DMA alignment, PAL, interlace, overscan, and pixel-fetch timing remain outside scope. Initial reset-created V=0 is outside the supported entered-scanline contract; do not describe its retained policy as verified hardware.

This Issue completes one scheduler sub-behavior. Preserve all inventory scopes: `cpu`, `bus`, `scheduler`, `dma`, `hdma`, `controllers`, `ppu-bg`, `ppu-offset`, `ppu-hires`, `ppu-mode7`, `ppu-objects`, `ppu-color`, `ppu-ports`, `ppu-display`, `spc`, `ipl`, `dsp-voices`, `dsp-noise`, `dsp-pitch`, `dsp-envelope`, `dsp-echo`, and `dsp-timing` remain partial; `ppu-raster` and `pal` remain unimplemented. None is fully verified. This does not complete Issue #3 or establish commercial-game compatibility.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Confirm and record the relevant Fullsnes detailed-event statement and Anomie register descriptions, with source links/revisions. Distinguish assertion timing from acknowledgement and CPU recognition. Resolve any contradictory evidence before implementing the affected requirement; do not preserve an unsupported earlier test contract.
- [ ] Implement combined HTIME=0 assertion at master H=10 on matching naturally entered scanlines. Remove that mode’s rollover assertion. Replace the two obsolete combined-zero expectations identified above while retaining H-only-zero and late-case controls as explicitly approximate behavior.
- [ ] Add original boundary tests named with a common `combined_zero_irq` prefix. Use fresh observations at H=0/9/10/11 for VTIME 0/1/224/225/239/240/241/261 across both naturally reached field parities. Clear earlier pending events before entering the target line, so acknowledgement cannot hide an erroneous H=0 event. Check nonmatching lines, unreachable VTIME=262/511, early reads preserving future delivery, pending retention across lines/fields and another matching event, and no duplicate after acknowledgement under the retained model convention.
- [ ] Derive expected clocks independently of production timing helpers. Include literal absolute assertion clocks: 1374 for initial-field V=1; 357378 and 714742 for successive natural V=0 events; 327370/684738 for V=240; and 328734/686098 for V=241. Exercise one-clock, irregular, and whole-interval advancement across ordinary/short lines and field rollover. Check final geometry and independently calculated audio sample counts; PCM partition equality establishes determinism only.
- [ ] Add six-clock CPU TIMEUP reads ending at H=0/9/10/11 and real fixed-A DMA reads from `$004211` into WMDATA across ordinary, field-rollover, and short-line boundaries. Under the existing DMA phases, starts at event−21/−20/−19 produce bit-7 records `[0,$80,0]`, `[$80,0,0]`, and `[$80,0,0]`. Verify transfer counts, addresses, destinations, acknowledgement, and final clocks/raster. Label coincident access results and DMA phases as model conventions, not physical timing verification.
- [ ] Add a real DMA transfer crossing the corrected event with an unmasked waiting CPU. Verify device advancement, retained IRQ, unchanged CPU PC/stack/instruction count during DMA, completed payload/counts, and one interrupt entry when CPU execution resumes. Preserve the existing interrupt-service convention.
- [ ] Add an original source-built integration guest in `crates/snes-core/tests/combined_zero_irq.rs`, configuring both HTIME bytes to zero, VTIME=240, SETINI=0, and combined mode before entering the target line. Naturally visit four fields, record H/V counters, field parity and TIMEUP acknowledgement, and self-check independently derived literal records in executed 65C816 code. Require explicit success/failure markers and bounded step/master-clock deadlines. The host must not inject beam position, IRQ state, or results. Record MIT authorship, construction, provenance, and clock derivations in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`.
- [ ] Demonstrate that the new boundary tests and guest fail behaviorally on the exact baseline and pass with the implementation. Record reproducible commands and actual results; compilation failures do not demonstrate the defect.
- [ ] Pass the focused new and existing scheduler tests, formatting, Clippy, and the full workspace suite:

  ```sh
  cargo test --locked -p snes-core combined_zero_irq
  cargo test --locked -p snes-core v_only_irq
  cargo test --locked -p snes-core horizontal_irq
  cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test ntsc_timing
  cargo test --locked -p snes-core --lib machine::ntsc_timing_tests
  cargo fmt --all -- --check
  cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
  cargo test --workspace --locked
  ```

  Preserve existing CPU/WAI, geometry, controllers, DMA/HDMA, PPU-port and audio assertions. Change another timing-derived expectation only with an independent derivation that preserves its original boundary coverage.

- [ ] Pass the existing licensed source-built hardware gates documented in [README validation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/README.md#validate):

  ```sh
  python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
  python3 tools/hardware-tests.py --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
  python3 tools/ppu-test.py --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
  ```

- [ ] Preserve existing game regressions and pass the normal browser gate against freshly built Wasm and pinned source-built games:

  ```sh
  python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
  python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
  npm --prefix web ci
  npm --prefix web run build
  npm --prefix web exec playwright install chromium
  npm --prefix web test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'
  ```

  Keep source/tool pins, licensing decisions, reproducible game hashes, replay routes, gameplay/music assertions, deadlines, and tolerances intact. Use README compiler-selection guidance where needed. Do not acquire commercial ROMs or firmware.

- [ ] Update README and a focused validation record with the supported domain, superseded combined-zero approximation, source qualifications, executed results, and remaining limitations. Limited passes must not be reported as full hardware accuracy or commercial compatibility.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
